question: What is the main tool used to see inside the tummy during a laparoscopy?

options.D: A tiny camera called a laparoscope

explanation: You got this! A laparoscope is a thin, lighted tube with a tiny camera on the end. It sends clear pictures of the inside organs to a TV monitor for the surgeon. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why do doctors often choose laparoscopy instead of traditional open surgery?

options.A: It guarantees zero risk of post-operative complications
options.B: It causes less pain and allows a faster recovery
options.C: It requires no special surgical equipment or training
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for general anesthesia

explanation: Spot on! Because the cuts (incisions) are very small, there is less damage to the body, less pain afterwards, and the patient gets back on their feet much quicker. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h1)

question: Which of these is a very common reason to perform a laparoscopy?

options.C: Repair of a fractured femur bone

explanation: Brilliant! Removing an appendix using tiny cuts (laparoscopic appendectomy) is a very common and safe way to treat appendicitis. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h2)

question: A patient has belly pain that normal scans cannot explain. What procedure is a doctor likely to suggest next?
explanation: Well done! When regular scans don't show the problem, a diagnostic laparoscopy lets the doctor look directly inside the abdomen to find out what is causing the pain. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h2)

question: For which patient condition is elective laparoscopy usually unsafe?

options.C: A history of a single childhood hernia

explanation: Correct! If a patient has a severe bleeding problem that hasn't been fixed, putting in surgical instruments can cause dangerous internal bleeding. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h3)

question: Why do past surgeries in the tummy make a new laparoscopy trickier?

options.A: Dense scar tissue increases the risk of organ injury during entry
options.B: The patient will require a much higher dose of antibiotics
options.C: Carbon dioxide gas cannot be absorbed through scarred tissue
options.D: Special cameras are unable to function in scarred abdomens

explanation: You're learning fast! Old surgeries leave behind scar tissue (adhesions) that can pull intestines closer to the tummy wall, making it easier to accidentally nick them during instrument entry. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h3)

question: Why is a patient told not to eat or drink (NPO) before a laparoscopy?

options.A: To prevent the surgical instruments from getting dirty
options.B: To ensure the patient loses weight before surgery
options.C: To stop the kidneys from producing urine
options.D: To reduce the risk of aspiration during anesthesia

explanation: Spot on! Keeping the stomach empty stops food or vomit from flowing up and entering the lungs while the patient is fast asleep under anesthesia. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h4)

question: As a nurse, what is one of your most important duties right before the patient goes for surgery?

options.A: Verifying that the informed consent form is signed
options.B: Teaching the patient how to change their wound dressing
options.C: Ordering a special post-operative hospital diet
options.D: Scheduling the patient's follow-up clinic appointment

explanation: Great job! Making sure the consent form is signed proves the patient understands the surgery, its risks, and has agreed to it before heading to the theater. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h4)

question: Why do surgeons pump carbon dioxide gas into the tummy during a laparoscopy?

options.A: To stimulate the patient's breathing rate
options.B: To create a working space and visualize organs clearly
options.C: To sterilize the surgical instruments automatically
options.D: To cool down the internal organs during the operation

explanation: Correct! The gas puffs up the tummy like a balloon, lifting the wall away from the organs so the surgeon has plenty of room to see and work safely. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h5)

question: What is a major equipment check the nurse must do before surgery starts?

options.A: Repairing broken video monitors during the surgical procedure
options.B: Manufacturing replacement trocars in the operating theater
options.C: Calibrating the hospital's central oxygen supply system
options.D: Ensuring all laparoscopic devices and light sources function properly

explanation: You got it! Checking cameras and lights beforehand prevents annoying and dangerous equipment failures right in the middle of the procedure. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h5)

question: What causes the shoulder pain some patients feel after a laparoscopic surgery?

options.A: Strain from lifting heavy objects in the recovery room
options.B: Tight bandages applied around the upper chest area
options.C: An awkward position maintained during prolonged walking
options.D: Residual carbon dioxide gas irritating the diaphragm

explanation: Spot on! Leftover gas can press against the diaphragm muscle, tricking the nerves into feeling like the pain is coming from the shoulder. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h6)

question: Why do nurses encourage patients to walk around soon after a laparoscopy?

options.A: It helps expel trapped gas and prevents blood clots
options.B: It ensures the patient can immediately leave the hospital
options.C: It replaces the need for prescribed pain medications
options.D: It prevents the surgical incisions from opening up

explanation: Brilliant! Early walking gets the blood moving in the legs to stop clots and helps the body clear out that trapped tummy gas faster. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h6)

question: Which of these is a rare but very serious complication unique to laparoscopy?
explanation: You're doing great! If the gas used to inflate the tummy accidentally gets directly into a blood vessel, it can travel to the heart or lungs, creating a dangerous gas embolism. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h7)

question: Which sign might mean a patient's bowel was accidentally injured during laparoscopy?

options.A: Mild itching around the small skin puncture sites
options.B: Severe, worsening abdominal pain and rigidity
options.C: Low-grade shoulder pain when taking a deep breath
options.D: Temporary hoarseness of the patient's voice

explanation: Spot on! If the bowel leaks contents into the tummy, it causes an infection (peritonitis) marked by severe pain and a tight, hard (rigid) belly. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h7)

question: What is the best home-care advice for a patient's small wound sites after laparoscopy?

options.A: Scrub the incisions vigorously with a rough sponge
options.B: Apply heavy grease daily to speed up healing
options.C: Keep the puncture sites clean and dry

explanation: Correct! Keeping tiny cut sites clean and dry keeps germs away and lets them heal nicely without any trouble. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h8)

question: A patient calls a few days post-surgery with a high fever and worsening belly pain. What should you advise?

options.A: Perform strenuous exercises to sweat out the fever
options.B: Return to the hospital promptly for medical evaluation
options.C: Eat a large heavy meal to restore body energy levels
options.D: Take an extra sleeping pill and wait until next week

explanation: You got it! Fever and worsening pain are warning signs of infection or internal injury, so the patient needs to be checked at the hospital right away. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h8)
